caption: Fig. 1. We improve DeepLabv3, which employs the spatial pyramid pooling module (a), with the encoder-decoder structure (b). The proposed model, DeepLabv3+, contains rich semantic information from the encoder module, while the detailed object boundaries are recovered by the simple yet effective decoder module. The encoder module allows us to extract features at an arbitrary resolution by applying atrous convolution.

caption: Fig. 3. 3 × 3 Depthwise separable convolution decomposes a standard convolution into (a) a depthwise convolution (applying a single filter for each input channel) and (b) a pointwise convolution (combining the outputs from depthwise convolution across channels). In this work, we explore atrous separable convolution where atrous convolution is adopted in the depthwise convolution, as shown in (c) with rate = 2.
description:
## Description:
This figure illustrates three types of convolutions used in image segmentation: depthwise convolution, pointwise convolution, and atrous depthwise convolution. Each panel shows a 3x3 convolution process. Panel (a) depicts depthwise convolution, where a single filter is applied to each input channel. Panel (b) shows pointwise convolution, which combines outputs from depthwise convolution across channels. Panel (c) represents atrous depthwise convolution, where atrous convolution is applied in the depthwise convolution with a rate of 2.

## Text in figure:
- (a) Depthwise conv.
- (b) Pointwise conv.
- (c) Atrous depthwise conv.
- rate = 2

caption: Fig. 4. We modify the Xception as follows: (1) more layers (same as MSRA's modification except the changes in Entry flow), (2) all the max pooling operations are replaced by depthwise separable convolutions with striding, and (3) extra batch normalization and ReLU are added after each 3 × 3 depthwise convolution, similar to MobileNet.
description:
This figure is a diagram showing the architecture of a modified Xception model for semantic image segmentation. It consists of three main flows: Entry flow, Middle flow, and Exit flow. Each flow includes a series of convolutional layers with varying numbers of filters and kernel sizes, as well as stride values. The architecture uses depthwise separable convolutions instead of max pooling and includes batch normalization and ReLU activations.

Entry flow: Conv 32, 3x3, stride 2, Conv 64, 3x3, Sep Conv 128, 3x3, Conv 128, 1x1, stride 2, Sep Conv 128, 3x3, stride 2, Sep Conv 256, 3x3, Conv 256, 1x1, stride 2, Sep Conv 256, 3x3, stride 2, Sep Conv 728, 3x3, Conv 728, 1x1, stride 2, Sep Conv 728, 3x3, stride 2.

Middle flow: Sep Conv 728, 3x3, Sep Conv 728, 3x3, Sep Conv 728, 3x3, repeated 16 times.

Exit flow: Conv 1024, 1x1, stride 2, Sep Conv 1024, 3x3, Sep Conv 1024, 3x3, stride 2, Sep Conv 1536, 3x3, Sep Conv 1536, 3x3, Sep Conv 2048, 3x3.

caption: Fig. 5. (a) mIOU as a function of trimap band width around the object boundaries when employing train output stride = eval output stride = 16. BU : Bilinear upsampling. In the examples, we adopt Xception as feature extractor and train output stride = eval output stride = 16.
